transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Start time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Rita Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Sara Velasquez (Lumos CISO), Tom Reynolds (Head of Infra), Priya Nair (Compliance), Alex Gomez (Cloud Eng)
---
Summary:
High-level SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture review; Lumos requested evidence around audit logs, retention, RBAC/SSO, KMS key management, data residency and controls mapping for their procurement/audit team. Redwood to share reports and provide Trust Center access; SE to map controls and follow up on technical deep-dive for private VPC options and KMS integrations.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um well do a quick run through of our security posture and then Ethan will go deeper on controls mapping and technical stuff. Sara, thanks for setting this up.
[00:10] Sara (Lumos CISO): Yeah thanks, Maya. Were evaluating a handful of providers, and security is the gating factor. We specifically need SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, audit logs with at least 12 months retention, RBAC w/ SSO, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
[00:25] Maya: Totally, thats exactly what we wanted to cover. Ethan, do you want to kick us off on the controls side?
[00:30] Ethan (Redwood SE): Sure, yeah. Quick overview: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering the typical security and availability criteria, and an ISO 27001 certificate. We maintain audit logs across the control plane and datastores; retention is configurable, default 90 days in hosted but we have enterprise options for extended retention up to 24 months via add-on. Note: some of our docs still say 1-year but the product side supports up to 24 months for Dedicated/Private.
[01:00] Tom (Lumos): Wait, you said default 90 days for hosted. Our procurement requires 12 months for production logs. Does that mean we need Dedicated or Private?
[01:10] Maya: Good question. For hosted customers, the standard package is 90 days, but for enterprise customers we offer extended retention as an add-on or via Redwood Dedicated where you can set retention policies to 12+ months. For strict residency requirements, Private (VPC/on-prem) is the usual route.
[01:25] Priya (Compliance): Can you confirm the log types captured? Application logs, admin actions, auth events, and model access events? We need tamper-evident audit trail.
[01:34] Ethan: Yes, we log admin actions, token-level access events, API calls, role changes, and model invocation metadata. For tamper evidence we use immutable write-once buckets for archived logs and we can provide SHA256 checksums on export. Slight caveat: some very high-cardinality model telemetry is sampled for performance; however all security-relevant actions are fully captured.
[02:00] Alex (Cloud Eng): About KMS: do you integrate with customer-managed keys in AWS KMS and GCP KMS? Do you support HSM?
[02:08] Ethan: We support AWS KMS and GCP KMS for key wrapping; for Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs or bring-your-own HSM behind the VPC. For hosted, we also support customer-managed key material via a delegated key mechanism, though some enterprise customers prefer Dedicated/Private for full key isolation.
[02:30] Sara: And what about encryption of in-flight and at-rest? TLS everywhere?
[02:34] Maya: TLS 1.2+ in transit with mutual TLS for certain internal services; at rest we use AES-256, and keys are managed in KMS. We can show the crypto-suite details in the trust center.
[02:45] Tom: On RBAC and SSO: we need SCIM provisioning and SAML 2.0, plus fine-grained roles down to model & route level. How granular is Redwoods RBAC?
[02:58] Ethan: RBAC is role-based with resource-level permissions. You can scope by project, model, and route. We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning; support for OIDC/Okta is available. Small note: some older screen docs say team-level only — that's an older doc. The runtime supports per-route policies and read/write/listen perms.
[03:20] Sara: Good. Procurement will want evidence — control mappings to SOC 2 criteria and ISO 27001 clauses. Do you provide a controls matrix?
[03:28] Maya: Yes, we have a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our controls to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 clauses. Ethan will attach a baseline template and annotate specific controls for Lumos.
[03:38] Priya: Also, we need to know about penetration testing cadence and third-party attestations.
[03:44] Ethan: We run annual third-party pentests and have a vulnerability disclosure program. Pentest letters and remediation summaries can be provided under NDA.
[03:52] Sara: Great. About trust center access: we will need to download the full SOC 2 report and ISO cert and have a secure way to get them — ideally via a limited-access trust center link.
[04:02] Maya: Well send a trust center invite. Its behind SSO; we can grant a view-only group to Lumos users. The invite typically expires after you download artifacts.
[04:12] Tom: For data residency: we have EU and US production tenants. Do you have regions and can we pin to AWS eu-west-1 and us-east-1?
[04:22] Ethan: Yes, hosted has region-aware clusters; you can pin workloads. For strict residency/residency controls the Private deployment in customer VPC gives full control of region. Hosted can be configured to store customer data in specific clouds/regions but some telemetry may cross regions for control plane unless dedicated. We can disclose specifics in the trust center.
[04:40] Alex: Regarding network isolation: do you support private endpoints, VPC peering, or private link equivalents?
[04:46] Ethan: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink-style endpoints for major cloud providers in Dedicated and Private offerings. For hosted customers we offer API gateways with IP allowlists and customer-managed TLS.
[04:58] Sara: One of our auditors asked about change management evidence and config drift detection. How do you manage infrastructure change control and approvals?
[05:06] Ethan: We use GitOps for infra changes, PR reviews, and require two approvers for prod rollout. We keep audit trail of deploys; recordings are in the pipeline logs. We can export change approvals as evidence for audits.
[05:22] Priya: Any certifications for your SOC 2 auditor or ISO registrar? We need the name and contact of the auditor/registrar listed on the cert.
[05:30] Maya: Yes, both are from accredited firms, names included on certs. We will send certified artifacts with the registrar details in the trust center package.
[05:40] Tom: A practical question: we plan to run a POC with 3 models and expect 200 qps during peak. For secure POC, should we do a hosted limited POC or spin up a Dedicated reserved pool?
[05:52] Ethan: For 200 qps and if you need enhanced logging/12-month retention + KMS integration, Dedicated is the middle ground. Hosted limited POC is faster but without longer retention or customer-KMS. If you can accept the standard hosted retention and managed keys, we can do hosted first then migrate.
[06:10] Sara: Our timeline: procurement wants vendor docs this week and a technical deep-dive next week. Can you meet those deadlines?
[06:17] Maya: Yes, we can provide docs this week and schedule a deep-dive next week.
[06:20] Rita (Redwood CSM): Ill coordinate the Trust Center invite and set permissions.
[06:24] [08:00] Ethan: One small point on logging: model call metadata includes prompt hashes and token counts but we avoid storing raw PII in logs by default; if customers send PII explicitly, that will be captured unless you use redaction hooks or client-side filtering. Just flagging that for compliance teams.
[06:45] Priya: Important to confirm retention and redaction options — can you do automated PII redaction at ingestion?
[06:51] Ethan: We offer optional redaction pipelines that can be enabled; for Private deployments you can run client-side filter before sending. We also provide guidance on prompt engineering to avoid PII.
[07:05] Tom: For audit logs export, can we push logs to our S3 with cross-account role?
[07:10] Ethan: Yes, we support cross-account log delivery to customers' S3/GCS buckets with role-based access. Thats often how customers maintain long-term audit archives.
[07:20] Alex: What's the SLA and how is incident reporting handled?
[07:25] Maya: For Dedicated customers we offer an SLA with incident severity definitions. Incident reporting uses our status page, pager duty integration, and we provide post-incident reports with timeline and RCA.
[07:36] Sara: On contract terms: we need contract language around security obligations, notification timelines for incidents, and right-to-audit clauses. Do you have standard clauses?
[07:44] Maya: We do. Our procurement/legal can provide standard security addendum language; well surface the right-to-audit flow and notification SLAs.
[07:52] Priya: For ISO controls mapping, can you map your controls to specific Annex A controls?
[07:57] Ethan: Yes, our ISO mapping references Annex A clauses and well include that in the controls spreadsheet.
[08:05] Tom: A small transcription note, Ive seen older docs referencing KV cash instead of KV cache in a readme — just a typo i guess, ha.
[08:12] Ethan: Yeah, well fix that in the public docs.
[08:16] Maya: Ok lets recap next steps — well (1) send SOC 2 and ISO cert in the trust center, (2) give Lumos access, (3) SE will prepare controls mapping, (4) schedule deep-dive for private deployment and KMS integration. Anything else?
[08:32] Sara: Could you also include previous pentest summary and auditor contact info in the trust package?
[08:36] Maya: Yes, under NDA we can share pentest letter and contact info.
[08:40] Priya: Also please include sample evidence artifacts for change management and access review.
[08:44] Ethan: Will do — Ill annotate the spreadsheet with pointers to the evidence artifacts location in the trust center.
[08:52] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. Well follow up with the links and schedule.
[08:56] Sara: Thanks all.
[09:00] End of call.
